Table of contents of an .rda file

Source: R/toc.R
rds_toc.Rd

Lists the objects in a file written by save(), with their types, classes, lengths, dimensions and where they lie in the decompressed stream, without building any of them. Nothing in the file is evaluated, and memory stays small however large the objects are.

Usage

rds_toc(x, kind = NULL)

Arguments

x

A path, raw vector or connection holding an .rda file.

kind

NULL to detect the kind of file, or one of "rds", "rda" and "lazyload" to insist on it.

Value

A data frame with one row per object, in the order save() wrote them:

  • name: the object's name.

  • type: its type, as typeof() names it.

  • class: its first class, or NA when it has no class attribute.

  • length: its length, as length() reports it for vectors and lists; NA where the stream does not record it (environments, functions, ALTREP objects).

  • dim: its dimensions as text, "3 x 4"; for a data frame, rows by columns; NA otherwise.

  • size: the bytes it takes in the decompressed stream.

  • offset: where it starts in the decompressed file, in bytes.

  • risky: whether it holds anything that can run code or reach outside the file: a finding of rds_scan() of severity "executes" or "reaches_out".

See also

Other inspection: rds_info(), rds_str()

Examples

f <- tempfile(fileext = ".rda")
x <- 1:10
cars <- mtcars
m <- matrix(0, 3, 4)
save(x, cars, m, file = f)
rds_toc(f)
#>   name    type      class length     dim size offset risky
#> 1    x integer       <NA>     10    <NA>  110     45 FALSE
#> 2 cars    list data.frame     11 32 x 11 3784    175 FALSE
#> 3    m  double       <NA>     12   3 x 4  143   3976 FALSE
